Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Ghana exports to China surge under zero-tariff policy Source : GNA 17 November 2026 5:10am President John Dramani Mahama ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Ghana’s exports to China rose sharply following the implementation of China’s zero-tariff policy, with imports from Ghana reaching US$290 million in June 2026.
The initiative is expected to expand market access for Ghanaian products and create opportunities for local exporters seeking to enter the Chinese market.
Mr Cong Song, Chinese Ambassador to Ghana, announced this at the 2026 Scholarship Alumni Association Reception and China-Ghana Zero-Tariff Forum in Accra.
He said bilateral trade between Ghana and China reached $14.12 billion in 2025, while Ghana’s exports to China amounted to $2.67 billion, representing a 33.9 per cent increase over previous years.
The forum, organised by the MOFCOM Scholars Alumni Association of Ghana (MOSAAG), formed part of a nationwide capacity-building initiative on China’s zero-tariff concession for African countries.
Mr Cong said the policy would reduce the cost of African products entering the Chinese market and improve their competitiveness.
He said China’s removal of tariffs on African goods would strengthen confidence in Africa’s economic prospects, support international trade and attract new investment.
“The zero-tariff policy is offered unilaterally, with no requirement for African countries to open their markets reciprocally. There is no ceiling on the volume of African exports to China.
“It comes with no political strings attached…For African countries, this means the door of opportunity to China’s mega-market of 1.4 billion people is wide open,” he said.
The Ambassador highlighted ongoing cooperation between Ghana and China across the mining value chain, including geological exploration, local processing, value addition and skills development.
He urged Chinese businesses operating in Ghana to comply with local laws and regulations and called for a conducive environment for investment.
Mr Cong encouraged MOSAAG to deepen public awareness of the zero-tariff initiative, identify export opportunities and help address implementation challenges.
“Let us join hands to harness the momentum of China’s zero-tariff treatment, and use the certainty of high-level bilateral opening-up and cooperation to offset the uncertainties in the global environment, injecting sustained and strong momentum into Africa’s development,” he said.
In a speech read on his behalf, Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Minister for Foreign Affairs, said the government remained committed to partnerships that supported industrialisation and economic transformation.
“Our interest is not to only to attract investment into the country; we seek partnerships that establish local production facilities, develop domestic supply chains, strengthen the skills of our workforce and create decent and sustainable jobs,” he said.
The Minister urged Ghanaian exporters to meet Chinese market requirements to fully benefit from the policy and deepen trade relations between the two countries.
He said the government would continue efforts to strengthen domestic production, improve competitiveness and create a business environment conducive to enterprise growth.
Mr Leonard Edem Cosmos, President of MOSAAG, said the forum sought to equip producers, agro-processors and small and medium-sized enterprises with the knowledge required to access the Chinese market.
“Knowing that duties have been removed is only the first step; knowing how to navigate sanitary and phytosanitary standards, packaging regulations, rules of origin, logistics, and Chinese buyer expectations is where real trade happens,” he said.
Mr Cosmos said the association would support capacity-building efforts, connect Ghanaian businesses with credible Chinese partners and promote effective implementation of the zero-tariff policy.
